The Church rightly asks for the coming of the Holy Spirit in the sacrifice, 35. Sacrifice is offered so that the Lord’s death may be proclaimed and commemorated, 618. God the Word offered himself as a sacrifice for us, 525. In the Old Testament, sacrifices offered for sins were called “sins,” 527.

**Sacrilege:** what it is, 425.

**Salvation** is freely given to the elect, 440. Everything contained in the divine utterances is spoken for the preservation or restoration of human salvation, 366. Everything pertaining to the advancement of human salvation is contained in the Old and New Testaments, 354. God alone can give to all whom he wills the means by which true salvation may be acquired, 178. How the statement concerning the wicked is to be understood: “They will marvel at the suddenness of an unexpected salvation,” 385.

**The necessity and efficacy of Christ’s blood**, 497, 498.

**Saints:** why they were predestined for the praise of the glory of God’s grace, [Col. 1011] 483. The saints do not fail through want, because their sufficiency is in him in whom there is no want, 164. Saints sin in one way, the wicked in another, 426. Why the saints in this life are subject to human weaknesses, 498. Why the righteous and saints are subjected to troubles, 424. In the saints God crowns the righteousness that he himself freely bestows and preserves in them, 1. To be holy in body and spirit means nothing other than preserving in action and thought what is holy, 153.

**To understand / to have a taste for.** To have a taste for earthly things is to love earthly things, 220.

**Wisdom** is the splendor of eternal light, 607. When it reaches from end to end, it surpasses both ends by its immensity, 97. Wisdom said that it was founded, demonstrating that its birth is unchangeable, 55. Created wisdom in the angels, 341.

**Sarah** sinned by laughing, but lightly, 426.

**Scammony** alone is harmful; mixed with other things, it is beneficial, 422.

Knowledge without charity is not holy knowledge, 464. In what ways knowledge of divine things is acquired, 5. That we may know and understand the things of God is God’s gift, 464.

**Scholasticus**, bishop, 269, 286.

**Scorpion.** In the body of the scorpion there is nothing that does not suggest the praise of the Creator, 421.

**Scripture.** Attention of heart ought to be devoted to the holy Scriptures, 189. Because of the unchangeability of the divine plan, Scripture speaks in the past tense of something whose fulfillment was awaited in the future, 348, 49. Fulgentius urges Galla to read the holy Scriptures, 162. Because of his ignorance of Scripture, Donatus did not find what to answer the Arians, 198. Praise of Thrasamund for his study of the Scriptures, 7. Euthymius is praised because he reads the Scriptures and frequents the Church, rejoices in the conversation of the saints, and avoids useless speeches, 360. If humility of heart is maintained in the divine utterances, no contradiction of the truth will be found, 97. One disputing about the Scriptures ought to seek the path of spiritual understanding, 47. What sort of mind ought to approach the divine utterances, 180, 465.

The devil is the sower, the nocturnal sower, 392. By the name of “seed” Paul designated each person’s works, 39. No one will receive anything other than what he sows, 90.

He is proved to serve two masters who believes that the divinity of the Son is different from that of the Father, 411. We ought to serve one another so that we may attain eternal life, 160. Silence is a sign of pride or doubtful faith, 143.

**Simeon**, an old man, a figure of the present age exhausted by old age, 72.

How closely sobriety, justice, and peace are joined, 426. Who lives soberly, 425.

**The sun of the human heart** is Christ, 376. A place is called “sunlit” because it is flooded with the light of the sun, 376. What it means to “loose Jesus,” 295.

**Form / appearance.** The grace of appearance will be given in place of the grace of faith, according to each person’s capacity, 253.

Hope excludes fear, 151. Hope, which drives out the vice of despair, is a gift of the Holy Spirit, 379. All hope must be placed in God’s mercy, 162. The devil captures the unwary through the vain hope of remission or through despair, 365.

## HOLY SPIRIT

Only the Holy Spirit, as the third person absolutely, is called “Spirit” in Scripture, 595. Although the Father and the Son are also “Spirit” absolutely, neither is called “Spirit” without an added designation, 595, 637. Testimonies that the Holy Spirit is God, 541 ff. When the Apostle says, “Glorify and bear God in your body,” he is speaking of the Holy Spirit, 204. The Holy Spirit is God because he is named in baptism, descended upon Jesus, and filled him, 617. The Holy Spirit is to be believed God because he is the pledge of our inheritance, 615. The Holy Spirit is the Spirit of both the Father and the Son, 523. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one Spirit with respect to nature; only the Holy Spirit is Spirit with respect to the property of person, 596. The Holy Spirit is referred to the Father and the Son, 235. The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, 523. The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Son as he proceeds from the Father, 252. The Holy Spirit proceeds wholly from the Father and wholly from the Son, ibid. It is proper to the Holy Spirit to proceed from the one who begets and the one begotten, 407, 408. For the Holy Spirit to hear is to proceed from the Father and the Son, 610, 611. For him to speak is to make himself ineffably present to our hearts by grace, 610. What it means that the Holy Spirit speaks not from himself, 611, 612.

The Holy Spirit has nothing less than the Father and the Son, 41. The Holy Spirit is in God by unity of nature and from God by the property of person, 336. The error against the equality of the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Son, 141. From Christ’s saying that demons are cast out by the Spirit of God, it does not follow that the Spirit is less than the Father or the Son, 342. The Holy Spirit is shown to be equal to the Father and the Son in that what the disciples could not bear while Christ was speaking, they were to bear through the gift of the Holy Spirit, 609. The Holy Spirit, although sent, is God, 333. The Holy Spirit is God, not less than the Father and the Son; he both contains all things and knows the secrets of the heart, 231. The equality of the Holy Spirit with the Father is shown by the fact that, although the angels see the face of the Father, they desire to gaze upon the Holy Spirit, [Col. 1012] 610. It does not prejudice the divinity of the Holy Spirit that we are said to have him from God, 597. The Holy Spirit knows the things of God because he is of the same nature, just as the human spirit knows what is in a human being because it is of the same nature, 235. We do not believe in the remission of sins, and so forth, in the same way as in the Holy Spirit, 656.

The Holy Spirit is immeasurable, 105. The Holy Spirit comes there by the bestowal of a gift where he is never absent in the greatness of his divinity, 617. The immensity of the Holy Spirit is shown by the fact that everywhere people are baptized in his name, 615. The Holy Spirit is naturally one and immeasurable God with the Father and the Son, 412. A creature cannot do the things attributed to the Holy Spirit in Scripture, 143. The Holy Spirit is Creator, not a creature, 24. The Holy Spirit has no place among God’s works, 648 ff. The divine Spirit, just as he created all things, so also fills all things, 204.

The Holy Spirit is the Comforter or Paraclete, 580. Through the Holy Spirit Christ was born and the Church was reborn, 26. The Holy Spirit has our bodies as his temple, just as the Father and the Son do; therefore he is one true God with the Father and the Son, 598. The manifestation of the Holy Spirit is his mission, 334. The Holy Spirit did not become either a dove or fire when he was signified by the appearance of such things, 626. The Holy Spirit did not assume the form of a dove as Christ assumed the form of a servant, 412. When the Church asks that the Holy Spirit be sent, it asks God to bestow the gift of charity and unity, 35. Why the Holy Spirit is said not to have been going to come unless Christ had departed, 569. Why the Holy Spirit is requested for the sanctification of the Church’s sacrifice, 34. Why only the sending of the Holy Spirit is requested in sacrifices, 32. Those who do not have the Spirit of God cannot understand divine things, 355. Gifts are of no benefit if the Spirit himself is not possessed, 35. The works of the Holy Spirit belong exclusively to the Trinity, 626.

How the Holy Spirit is said to groan or make requests, 584, 628. He does not speak from himself, 611. He is sent by the Father and the Son, 612, 613 ff. The Holy Spirit is free, 625. In what way the Spirit is manifold, 621, 622. By the name “Spirit,” his gifts are sometimes designated, 621. The seven Spirits in Revelation, chapter 1, verse 4; what they signify, ibid. and 622. Where there is charity, there is the Holy Spirit, 35. The pledge of the Spirit is God’s gratuitous gift, 474. The comparison of the sun with healthy or diseased eyes shows that the Holy Spirit, though one, is received differently by different people, 34. The Holy Spirit is manifold not in himself but in his gifts, 621. Those who are separated from the unity of the Church’s body lose this Spirit, 3. The Holy Spirit is one, 614, and immeasurable, ibid. and 615.

The fruit of the Spirit, 485, 455. How the Holy Spirit is said to be grieved and the Son of God trampled underfoot, 430. The Spirit of God cannot in himself be grieved, nor can the Son be trampled underfoot, 481. We are the temple of the Holy Spirit, as of the Father and the Son, 141, 204. We are the temple, sacrifice, and priests of the Holy Spirit, as also of the Father and the Son, 597. The Holy Spirit is said to groan or make requests because he causes us to groan or make requests, 585. The Holy Spirit makes us groan by making us grieve over our iniquity, ask forgiveness, and desire righteousness, 585. The servant who hid the money received from his Lord did not possess the spiritual pledge, 474.

The gifts of the Holy Spirit—that is, tongues, prophecy, knowledge of the sacraments, faith, distribution of possessions to the poor, and even the burning of the body itself—can be possessed without good will, 183. Whether and how the Spirit is the Father and the Son, 595. The gifts of the Holy Spirit can be diminished and increased, but not the Spirit himself, 34. Under the name “Spirit,” spiritual gifts are sometimes signified, 33. The Holy Spirit has a measure in us, but not in Christ, 250, 251. The seven Spirits before the throne, 622. In spirits no difference of sex can be found, 600. Rational spirits, although they are not locally in a place, nevertheless pass from place to place, 615. Elijah’s twofold spirit, 621. “Spirit” is sometimes used for “wind,” 581.

The splendor of the saints means not the prophecies of the prophets but the brightness of the resurrection, 64.

**Assistance.** In the assistance of the Spirit there is not a ministry of servitude but the aid of divine majesty, 628. The Holy Spirit is said to assist and administer, not to minister, 582 ff.

**Pride:** whence it took its beginning, 14. Pride is the beginning of sin, ibid. Pride is called the beginning of every sin so that every sin may be shown to sprout from it as from a root, 172. Through pride human beings fell back into death, 14. Why God resists the proud, 15. Blessed Paul, saying, “O man, who are you?” and so forth, did not fail in his answer but restrained, by a useful rebuke, the pride of hardened flesh, 475. The four kinds of proud people are the four-horse chariot by which the devil is carried, 173. The devil injects pride if he cannot take away the virginity of the flesh, 171. That pride by which other people are despised as sinners by those who seem righteous to themselves is condemned in the Pharisee, 173. Pride is clearly detected when sin is openly committed, 172. Those who place themselves above the poor to whom they distribute gifts, or congratulate themselves on having despised riches, sin more gravely than those who retain some boastfulness in their hearts over possessing them, [Col. 1013] 160. The pride by which someone attributes to his own powers what God gives is more deeply rooted than the pride by which someone does what God condemns, 189. Pride is much more dangerous when iniquity is cunningly practiced under the disguise of righteousness, 172.

**Supererogation.** The various opinions of the holy Fathers concerning the supererogation of blessed Paul, 39.

**Creed:** what the word signifies, 652. What it is and why it was established, ibid. In the Creed the origin and distinction of the divine persons are indicated, ibid. and following. When the Father is called “almighty” and “creator” in it, this is to be understood of the whole Trinity, ibid. All the articles of the Creed are enumerated, 655, 656.

## T

**The temple of God** is also called the house of God, 592. In the temple God is served through prayer and sacrifice, 641. The faithful are the temple of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, 592.

**Temporal things.** Temporal affairs are uncertain, 467. How vain human concern over temporal affairs is, 467.

**Time.** The present time is the acceptable time, 389. The present is the time of salvation; the future, of recompense, 388. Now is the time for the straw to be changed into wheat, 402. Now the Lord can be found and therefore must be sought, 403. The present is the time of work; the future, of reward, 397. There is one time of sowing and another of recompense, 390.

Darkness is the absence of light; silence, the absence of voice, 423. How darkness and light, voice and silence, and so forth, are contrary, ibid. Why darkness occurred when Christ died, 567.

**Temptation.** Human mortality is permitted to be wearied by temptation so that, when it finds no strength of virtue in itself, it may quickly turn to seek the help of divine mercy, 179. When the weakness of the flesh strikes the mind, the soul should turn to the help of divine mercy, 149.

**Earth.** A human being would not go into the earth in the flesh if the earth had not been made so through sin, 300.

**Tertullian** said that the soul was not spirit but body, 496. He said that God was body, ibid.

**Testament.** There is one faith of the New and Old Testament, 268. No one should therefore reject the Old Testament because he sees that its sacraments have ceased, 267. In both Testaments it is commanded that we not sin, and we are ordered to persist in good works, 550. Certain sacraments of the Old Testament were God’s words promising, 265. The faithful words of God in the Old Testament promise; in the New, God’s holy works fulfill what he had promised, 265. Both Testaments are designated in Scripture under the names of the old and new friend, 267. The new wine is the New Testament, ibid. How it grows old so that it may be drunk with sweetness, ibid.

The writings of Theodore of Mopsuestia are anathematized, 281.

**Theodosius**, the emperor, held John the Theban monk in the highest honor, 478.

Our treasure is to be placed in heaven, 549. We store up treasure where we direct our love, 549.

**The confession of Saint Thomas:** when commanded to test the reality of the wound, he acknowledges the Lord God, 297, 298. Saint Thomas called Christ God, 200.

**Fear.** God is to be feared; kings are to be honored, 70. Even the righteous ought to fear God, 365. Divine Scripture commands the righteous to fear in such a way that it does not make sinners despair, 366. These words of Paul, “Work out your salvation with fear and trembling. For it is God …,” commend the justice and mercy of God, ibid. The good are commanded to remain in the fear of the Lord, 365. The Apostle’s example of fearing lest he become reprobate ought to terrify everyone, 391. Fear is the guardian of received salvation, 366. Evil fear among worldly people, 467.

Thunder is the preaching of the Gospel, 581.

**God’s handing over:** 325. How he hands over the good and the wicked, ibid.

**Tradition of the holy Fathers**, 287.

**Thrasamund** was a king, 69. King Thrasamund wrote to Fulgentius a lengthy volume containing heretical material, ibid.

Tribulation benefits Christians so greatly that through it our spirit becomes a sacrifice to God, 196. Tribulation, weakness, and distress are signs of God’s goodwill, 195.

**Thirty.** Once a period of thirty years has been completed, no one is permitted by human laws to reclaim what was taken away, 192.

## TRINITY

“Trinity” is the name apart from which we know no other, and by invoking which we are freed from death, 67, 68. The Trinity is the supreme and unchangeable good, 526. Right faith concerning the Trinity, 502. The Trinity is naturally one true God, 411. One God is the Trinity, yet three persons, 407. There is one nature in God and three persons, 329, 330. The Holy Trinity is one true and unchangeable God, 502. The Trinity of persons in God was revealed to Isaiah, 50. Testimonies concerning the Trinity, 540, 541. The Trinity refers to the persons; unity to the nature, 503. The Trinity is proved from the Scriptures, 331. It is also proved from Abraham’s vision, ibid. The Trinity is indicated when it is said, “Let us make man in our image and likeness,” 352, 353. Cyprian’s testimony concerning the unity of the Trinity, 68. Another example is drawn from the unity of Christ’s person in two natures, [Col. 1014A] 248, 249. It is proved by the example of the human soul, in which there are memory, understanding, and will, 352, 353 ff. Another example is drawn from different natures in one person, namely, in a human being, 356. In creatures there is a trinity in unity; therefore much more in God, 335. When the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are named, not three natures but three persons must be understood, 298. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are called the Trinity because they are three persons, and one God because they are one substance, 19. The nature of the three persons is not one in the same way as the nature of three human beings is one, 233. When it is said, “one God, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit,” one nature is to be understood; when “Trinity” is said, three persons, 198.

The equality of the persons, 330. Testimonies concerning the equality of the Father and the Son, 537, 538. The Son and the Spirit are true God, as is the Father, 521. Two fathers differ from each other more than the Father and the Son do, 52. What is naturally the Father is the Son and is the Holy Spirit, 407. In what respect the Father is greater than the Son, 533. Holy Scripture presents to all the faithful the Son as true God, just as it presents the Father as true God, 201. There is one royal power belonging to the three persons because there is a natural unity of those who reign; royal power is not bestowed by grace but exists by nature, 200. The Son or the Holy Spirit does not reign with the Father as an inferior with a superior, 261. None of the three persons has anything less than the other two, since in each person the divinity is so full that it is one in the three persons and wholly present in each individual person, 252. True faith proclaims the eternal power and divinity of the Father in such a way that it believes in the eternal power and divinity of the Son and the Holy Spirit, 140.

The Church sacrifices to the Trinity and not to the Father alone, 363 ff. All religious service is inseparably offered to the three persons because in the three there is an inseparable and unchangeable nature, 632. The whole Trinity is invoked in one person, 629. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit have one power and divinity, 241. The Trinity is immortal and invisible in a manner different from an angel or the soul of a human being, 653 ff. Neither the Son nor the Holy Spirit is a creature, because each is joined to the Father in the sacrament of baptism, 64.

The Father is light, as is the Son, 60. The Father is day, as is the Son, 61. The Father is in the Son, light in light, ibid. Whoever thinks that there is a difference of divinity in the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit believes in another God rather than one God, 204. Greater and lesser are not spoken of in the Trinity, 407. Not only is the Trinity God, but each person is God, 330. Not only does the Trinity fill all things, but each person in the Trinity does so, 345. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit work inseparably because they are inseparable, 236. The works of the Trinity are inseparable, 341, 652. The Trinity is inseparable, 340 ff. The inseparability of the Trinity is asserted from Ambrose and Augustine, 237. The Trinity is inseparable because it itself causes us to adhere inseparably to God through love, 239. Just as the Trinity is inseparable, so the three persons are inseparable, 230. Each person in the Trinity, in those names by which it is spoken of in relation to itself, is itself what it is naturally declared to possess, 241.

The immensity of the Trinity, 230, 409. The whole Trinity is immeasurable, 105. The Trinity alone is immeasurable, 615. The whole Trinity is everywhere, 33. The whole Trinity is wholly in each creature and wholly in all creatures, 230. Thus the whole Trinity dwells in each as wholly as it dwells in all, 109. In what way it is said to ascend or descend to us, 101. He is thought to be present everywhere who is named everywhere in baptism for the purpose of sanctifying, 110. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit dwell in us not by a local dwelling but an immeasurable one, 109. The immensity of each person is as great as that of the three persons naturally, 407. In the Trinity there is no particular distinction because there is no composition, 71, 72. What absurdity follows if the Trinity’s indwelling is believed to be local, 109.

The incomprehensibility of the Trinity surpasses everything we can think or understand just as it surpasses everything that we are, 88. Traces of the Trinity in creatures, 334. The Trinity alone can reveal itself because it alone can fully know itself, 90. The image of the Trinity in the human soul, 552, 553, 600. The human mind does not have personal distinction, although it bears an indication of the Holy Trinity, 356. An indication of the Trinity in fire, 606. Humanity was made in the image of the Trinity, 204. The Father and the Son cannot be known or exist without the Holy Spirit, 99. The image of the persons of the Trinity in the two natures of one human being, 418. The advent of the Trinity shows not mobility but the piety of God who comes, 100. Just as there is one manifestation, so there is one revelation of the whole Trinity, 99.

The Holy Trinity is the creator of all things, 512, 522. God’s works are common to the whole Trinity, 141. The whole Trinity made the form of a servant that the Only-Begotten assumed, 247. The name and function of teacher belong to the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, 582. The name and function of judge belong to the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, 524. Not everything that the whole Trinity does is also received by the whole Trinity, 352. In every gift the gift of the Holy Trinity is one, just as in every work the function of the Holy Trinity is one, 609. Right faith concerning the most holy Trinity is especially necessary for a Christian, 407, 502. We are the temple of the Trinity, [Col. 1015] 592. The Catholic faith concerning the Trinity, 544, 545. It will benefit nothing to have run toward the truth while erring concerning the Trinity, 71.

In the Trinity there are certain properties belonging to the persons, 407. What they are, 587. Personally, the one who is the Father is not the Son; nor is the one who is the Son the Holy Spirit, 407. The Father is one, the Son another, yet neither is another God, 552.

**Sorrow** is twofold, 132. Sorrow conceived for evil deeds is salutary, ibid. Sorrow over the loss of temporal comfort is deadly, ibid. Hope of the resurrection does not permit sorrow over the death of the faithful, 151. Both the mourning of the humble and the joy of the proud will not be without future recompense, 196. What does it mean to go about sorrowful all day? 179.

## U

**Unity:** that it should be maintained, 227. God made the multitude of believers one heart and soul because the Spirit of the Father and the Son is one and, with the Father and the Son, is one God, 37. Christ consecrated the mystery of peace and unity at his table, 227. The word “womb” signifies nature, 64. “From the womb, before the morning star, I begot you”: the Arians understood this of a temporal birth, because a carnal womb cannot be believed to exist in God, ibid.

## V
Vessels of mercy and vessels of wrath: who are they? 274. Those who possess ecclesiastical or secular rank are not vessels of mercy, nor are those who do not possess it vessels of wrath, ibid. Why they are called vessels of wrath and vessels of mercy, 21. A foolish opinion held by some concerning the making of vessels of dishonor and honor, 475. God’s gratuitous love distinguishes vessels of wrath and dishonor from vessels of God’s mercy, 475, 477. Greater ecclesiastical or secular rank does not make anyone a vessel of honor, 475, 476. In vessels of wrath, natural guilt is nourished by proud knowledge, 457. In vessels of mercy, natural guilt is dissolved by faith and charity, ibid. Why the Apostle calls the saints vessels of mercy, not of justice, 437. Why vessels of mercy are not called vessels of justice, 21. Why the reprobate are vessels of wrath, not of guilt, 22. The saints are not vessels of dishonor merely because they suffer dishonor in this age, 479. How God is merciful toward vessels of mercy, 21. Through a change of evil life, vessels become vessels of honor, 482. Vessels of mercy prepared for glory—not present glory, but future glory, 274. It is not rank but charity that makes vessels of mercy, 274. Who are the vessels of dishonor in the Church, 480. God begins his judgment against vessels of wrath by abandonment and completes it by torment, 22. Both in vessels of wrath and in vessels of mercy, personal iniquity preceded, 21. What the destruction is for which God fitted the vessels of wrath, 22. Why destruction is repaid to the vessels of wrath, ibid.

Venerius, deacon, 269, 434.

**The Word.** When “Word” is named, the distinct person of the Father and the Son is shown; when the Word is called “God,” the one substance of both is shown, 355. The name “God” in the Word expresses the truth of a natural name, not a merely titular one, 74. The Father has one Word, 417. He is no less perverse who denies that the Word of God exists in God than one who refuses to confess that it possesses a human soul, 51. We are not in God in the way the Word is, 50. The Word of God is from God; through the unity of nature it is in God, and through that same unity it is one God with him, 51. The generation of the Word is indescribable, not unknowable, 53. The humanity of the Word is said to have been made, not its divinity, 82. The Word of God was manifested through the substance of flesh, just as a human word is manifested through bodily speech, 417. The two natures of the Word of God are neither confused nor separable, 524. No place is coeternal with the Word, ibid. Faith in the Incarnation is hearing the Word of God, 417. In the first three statements of John’s Gospel, the eternal birth of the Word, its personal and unconfused property, and the undivided substantial unity of the Father and the Son are shown, 74. The Word is as great as the mind with the word, 50. When the mind thinks, it generates a word, ibid. The mind has within itself a word which it generated from its own substance by thinking, 50. The word possesses nothing less than the mind from which it is born. The word is not separated from the mind spatially, ibid. What does it mean to speak against the Holy Spirit? 378. Who speak against the Holy Spirit, 378, 379. Who are free from speaking against the Holy Spirit, 379. The word against the Holy Spirit is forgiven neither in this age nor in the age to come, ibid. The Word of God is a good adversary, 387. The Word of God, which is cast away, is the adversary of the human being, 387. The word benefits God’s stewards: while they distribute it, they hear it humbly, 361. To whom are those who hear the word without fruit similar? 360.

**Truth.** Only that which is naturally true divinity is naturally truth, 202. Every creature is a true creature, but not truth, ibid. Truth is desired more worthily than the expansion of power, 71. The pursuit of truth is right and never fruitless, ibid. One must always cling to truth, 5. The more secretly truth speaks, the sweeter it is, ibid. To do truth is to perform the work of truth, 8. Truth never lies, 190. Truth neither deceives nor is deceived, 5. It itself enlightens, assists, and confirms us so that we may obey and consent to truth, 5. Whom God makes come to the knowledge of truth, 488. People are saved in this: that they attain to the knowledge of truth, 489. To hold the truth of God is to worship the one God, 201. To turn the truth of God into a lie is to serve the creature, 11. The truth of nature is never deprived of the truth of its name, 74. The communication of truth must be denied to no one, 70. Whoever responds to those who ask with what pertains to the faith of truth loves and honors kings, 70, 71.

Those are without a wedding garment who are without good works, 402.

Our way is the present life, 387. The way of God is right faith, 76. The way of God is justice, mercy, and truth, ibid. On God’s way one walks not with bodily but with mental progress, ibid. He is deceived who thinks that he will reach life by the broad way, 386.

**Victims.** In the Old Testament, victims were offered to the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, 525. In carnal sacrifices there was a signification of Christ’s flesh, 525.

Victor, bishop, 569, 226.

Victor, another bishop, ibid.

**Victory.** In this life we conquer the adversary if we fight with tears, prayers, and continual humility of heart, 179.

Letter of Victor to Saint Fulgentius, 208. Victor asks Saint Fulgentius to respond to the discourse of Fastidiosus, 209.

Victorianus, bishop, 269, 286.

To have seen in the Father, in the Son, is to proceed from him, 611.

**Widow.** From the benefits with which God favored Judith and Anna, he showed that widowly continence is pleasing to him, 159. What the entire people of the Israelites could not do, the holy widow accomplished through the virtue of chastity, 159. Christ deemed it worthy to be preached through a widow’s tongue, because widowly continence follows virgin sanctity at a lower degree, ibid. By Judith’s exaltation, God showed how pleasing widowly continence is to him, 159. The widow’s state is an opportunity for increasing virtue, 154. Holy widows always sought Christ, 159. Judith is the example of widows in the Old Testament, and Anna in the New, 158, 159. What practices a widow should observe in daily life, 158. How a widow should conduct herself in eating, ibid. A widow’s foods should not be the same as those of a married woman, 157. What the clothing of widows should be like, ibid.

The feast of Saint Vincent is celebrated everywhere in the Church, 572.

Vindicianus, bishop, 269, 286.

Viper flesh is used against viper bites, 422. Viper offspring are born by tearing apart the entrails of those that give birth, 373. For vipers, giving birth is the same as perishing, 372. Heretics and schismatics are like vipers, ibid.

The word “virginity” is derived from the name of virtue, 165. A virgin is so called as though she were *virago*, 165. She is called *virago* because she was taken from a man, ibid. The word “virgin” is derived from *vir* (“man”), just as the name “Christian” is derived from Christ, 166. Donations for the building up of the Church are found to be called by their proper names; the sanctity of bodily integrity, however, is called virginity so that it may be shown that the perfection of true virtue is present there, 167. Holy virginity is as far above holy marriage as better things are above good things, heavenly things above earthly things, security above tribulation; and just as the likeness of animals is distinguished from the imitation of angels, so holy marriage differs from holy virginity, 168. Virginity is a matter of the will, not of necessity, 39. Paul gives counsel, not a command, concerning virginity, ibid. A corrupted virgin deceived the first man; an incorrupt virgin conceived the second man, 554. Holy virginity is adorned by Christ so that it may remain beautiful, and crowned so that it may reign gloriously, 165. Holy virginity spiritually marries Christ, ibid. Holy virginity is made fruitful by Christ so that it may persevere undefiled, ibid. Christ is the fruit, adornment, and gift of holy virginity, ibid. Holy virginity bore Christ, ibid. Christ is the bridegroom of all holy virgins, ibid. Christ is not only the bridegroom but also the Lord of virgins, 173. Under the name of eunuchs, through Isaiah, God promises virgins a better place in his house, 167. In faithful married women and widows, the Church possesses only spiritual virginity, 166. The Church has received the greater grace of the gift in those members in whom she is called spiritually virgin, so that it also possesses the integrity of bodily virginity, ibid. The reward of virginity will be great in the future, 169. Nothing is better than bodily integrity, 164. A virgin may not marry after making a vow, 148. Virginity makes one more like the angels than like human beings, 169. The holy virgin’s pursuit is justice, piety, faith, charity, patience, and gentleness, 173. The devil spreads spiritual snares for spiritual virgins, 171. The union of virginity with humility is the highest perfection in this life, 164. A virgin must not turn aside either to the right or to the left, 169. Bodily virginity without humility cannot reach Christ, 176. A virgin cannot be united to Christ except through humility of heart, 173. True humility is the inner virginity of virginity, 175. For virginity dedicated to God to remain intact, just as bodily integrity is guarded, humility of heart must be guarded much more carefully, 173. Bodily virginity, even when dedicated to God, is of no benefit unless virginity of heart is present, 171. The devil strives to take away bodily virginity through a human being, but virginity of heart through himself, 171. If the devil cannot destroy bodily virginity, he attempts to take away spiritual virginity, 171. Christ’s virgin must not despise other Christian women because of her own condition, 173. Christ’s virgin must not flatter herself because others are in greater danger, but must humbly grieve over her own weakness, 174. Because Christ is always living, the affection of his brides must therefore always live in their hearts, 158. Christ’s virgin must flee the pleasures of the flesh, but above all pride, 169, 170. Christ wishes to see the flesh of his bride subdued, 157. In his brides Christ loves the beauty of the soul, not of the flesh, ibid. The clothing of virgins should testify to inner chastity, 170. A virgin’s adornment is to preserve the good of virginity no less in mind than in flesh, 169. A virgin is neither truly chaste nor faithful to Christ if she seeks to please the people more than the bridegroom, 170. A virgin who seeks bodily adornment strips her soul of the splendor of virtues, ibid.

Blessed Virgin, Mother of God, 287. The Blessed Virgin is properly Θεοτόκος (*Theotokos*, “God-bearer”), 278. Mary’s virginity, 292. The Virgin received from the one whom she conceived the gift of incorruptible fruitfulness and fruitful integrity, ibid.

A man is called *vir* from virtue, 165.

**Virtue.** The human being was made in such a way that he could possess virtue, 188. When you think about the perfection of virtues, do not consider what others possess less of than you, but what you possess less of than you ought already to possess, 174. There must be continual progress toward virtue, 156. Divine virtue is food for angels and medicine for human beings, 90. This virtue restored the human being and preserved the angel, ibid.

**Life.** A just life will benefit one in the future life, 382. A person’s way is his life, 562. Whoever lives well enters the way of truth, ibid. Whoever lives badly follows the way of error, ibid. Who live justly? 382, 426. A long or short life benefits unbelievers nothing, 152. It is not a long life but a good one that benefits, 153. He does not possess life who remains either in crime or in unbelief, 197. He possesses life who does not withdraw from the bosom of Mother Church, ibid. This life is our way, in which we must always make progress, 178. In this life sorrow and comfort are mingled; not in the future life, 432. In this mortal life there cannot be complete security, 179. From the end of this life depends the beginning of eternal life, 389, 394. Both the good life and eternal life are in Christ and from Christ, 9. What is old age? An unblemished life, 153. We shall receive the blessed life if we regard ourselves as dead to this life, 187. If eternal life comes to an end, all Christian labor is useless, 93. When God gives eternal life, he perfects what he began by justifying, 9. God gave human beings the time for acquiring eternal life only in this life, 516. The origin of an evil life is original sin, 515. Iniquity pollutes life through evil habits, 372.

**Will.** What is the will? 553. Whatever a person knowingly says, he says willingly, 354. The will in itself has the capacity to desire good or evil spontaneously, 463. Unless the will is changed by God, it either always desires evil or never desires good, 461. A person cannot possess the beginning of a good will from himself, 515. The beginning of a good will is from God, 300. A good will is given by God, 306. The will is good when it is preceded by God’s gift, and it remains good when it is not deprived of his assistance, 273. The will is given by him by whom it is prepared, [Col. 1018] 7. Why the will is said to be prepared by the Lord, ibid. God prepared the good will and its action by predestination, ibid. The human will must accompany grace, 469. The will cannot love the good unless it has received from God the grace of discernment and charity, 463. When we do God’s will, we do it willingly; but, so that we may do it, he himself works in us what is pleasing before him, 462. The human will is continually governed and directed by God, 450, 451. The good will begins in faith and is perfected by charity, 465. Faith and charity exist in a person and benefit a person because he voluntarily receives them, 465. The difference among God’s gifts must be attributed solely to the divine will, 453. The human will, unless changed by grace, either sins unknowingly or heaps its vice upon vice through transgression, 454. No one can recover a good will by his own powers, 454. What else is signified by the wicked servant’s being ordered to be bound hand and foot except that the guilt of an evil deed is shown to be punished in the hands, and the inclination of an evil will in the feet? 403. An evil will is the punishment of evil, 14. God is the ordainer of evil wills, not their author, 20. The best Creator did not make an evil will, 15. Whether a will is good or harmful must be judged by the end of the matter in question, 184. The will of the Almighty must necessarily be fulfilled in all things, 488. How can Christ be said to have willed what he did not will for Jerusalem? 383. Not even the impious dare say that the divine will can be changed or its power overcome by any adversity, 484. God does not will those to be saved and to come to the knowledge of truth from whom he conceals the mystery of his knowledge, 486. Why does God punish the evil will of human beings? 440. To do God’s will is nothing other than to perform the works which his will inspires in us and works in us, 8.

A vow should concern lawful things pertaining to progress toward a better life, 521. For one who has not vowed, it is not a sin if he does not fulfill it, 147. The use of lawful things remains lawful as long as renunciation has not been vowed, 147. Vows must be fulfilled to God without excuse, ibid. One who vows without his whole heart is bound by the vow, and is all the more culpable because he approaches God deceitfully, 148. A vow made in tribulation must be fulfilled, 147. What a person by vowing to God voluntarily takes away from himself in the matter of continence, necessity thereafter permits no one to use with impunity, 148. Nothing may be retained or reclaimed from a vow, 149. Satan filled the hearts of Ananias and Sapphira because each retained part of what had been vowed, ibid. Those who have vowed continence cannot marry, 520, 521. A vow of continence binds virgins and widows as well as married women if they make it by mutual consent, 148. Vows of continence bind under mortal sin even when made by married women with their husbands’ consent, 521. After a vow has been made by married persons, every sexual union is illicit, 148. Married persons do not have the freedom to vow as a widow or virgin does, ibid. A married person cannot vow without the consent of the spouse, ibid. A spouse’s vow without the consent of the other spouse is rash, 149. It is the same as if a married person attempted to profess continence, as if someone attempted to give alms from another’s property or to offer a sacrifice from it, 148. A vow made with the consent of both parties cannot be violated with impunity, ibid. Nothing may be retained or reclaimed from a vow, 149.

**Voice.** What voice is it whose knowledge the Spirit possesses? 231. The removal of the voice does no harm to one who confessed as long as he was able, 221.

Christ alone opened the womb of his mother, 301.
